s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological syndrome with urinary retention and progressive gait disturbances
salient_findings: Enhancing intramedullary mass involving the conus medullaris
key_facts: Intramedullary mass involving the conus medullaris at the L1–L2 level on MRI

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological syndrome with urinary retention and progressive gait disturbances
salient_findings: Enhancing intramedullary mass involving the conus medullaris
key_facts: Intramedullary mass involving the conus medullaris at the L1–L2 level on MRI

differentials: Cavernous hemangioma of the spinal cord
per_call: Cavernous hemangioma of the spinal cord

shortlist.label: Schistosomiasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of drinking unsafe water and eosinophilia

shortlist.label: Spinal cord abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Acute neurological syndrome with urinary retention

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of acute urinary retention, progressive gait disturbances, and ataxia, combined with the presence of 450 eosinophils on routine blood tests and an intramedullary mass on MRI, are most consistent with eosinophilic meningomyelitis, particularly given the history of drinking unsafe water which could suggest a parasitic infection

rejected.label: Schistosomiasis
rejected.why: While schistosomiasis is a possibility given the patient's location and history of drinking unsafe water, the presence of an intramedullary mass and eosinophilia are more suggestive of eosinophilic meningomyelitis

rejected.label: Spinal cord tumor
rejected.why: The acute onset of symptoms and the presence of eosinophilia are not typical of a spinal cord tumor

rejected.label: Spinal arteriovenous malformation
rejected.why: The MRI findings could suggest an arteriovenous malformation, but the clinical presentation and eosinophilia are more consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process

rejected.label: Spinal cord abscess
rejected.why: The presence of an intramedullary mass could suggest an abscess, but the lack of other signs of infection, such as fever or elevated white cell count, makes this less likely
